thread:
maya (AE): HarborPay reached out — they're planning to replace CompetitorX. Requesting a short POC for parity + cost impact. Can we scope blockers?
diego (Solutions): good call. What are their non-negotiables?
maya (AE): 1) label parity on a 40-prompt chargeback detection set
2) predictable token billing comparison
3) security questionnaire answered + IP allowlist
4) staged rollout plan with rollback
anya (Infra): for tail latency they'd likely need Dedicated in their region. We should offer both hosted and Dedicated numbers.
lee (Security): send their questionnaire; I'll prefill SOC2, KMS options, and logging retention. Any EU residency notes?
maya (AE): yes EU data residency required.
ravi (Prod): did a quick adapter prototype. Main diffs: stop-sequence handling and CompetitorX's newline-trimming. Example behavior: Competitor returns minimal JSON without closing newline which our parser flags. We can add a postprocess fixer for the POC.
diego (Solutions): postprocess rules sound good. Keep it minimal: 1) ensure JSON closed, 2) normalize whitespace, 3) enforce required keys. If still invalid, surface parity_note.
anya (Infra): adapter adds CPU; estimate +7% on high QPS. We'll include both raw and adapter throughput in the report. Staging egress IPs: 52.6.10.11, 52.6.10.12.
maya (AE): they want cost for PAYG vs 3mo reserved. Can finance produce sample numbers based on token mapping?
diego (Solutions): ask HarborPay to upload 40 representative prompts; I'll run tokenization and return a CSV mapping Competitor tokens -> Redwood token estimate. Also will produce prompt engineering tips to reduce divergence.
lee (Security): HarborPay needs CMK and HSM custody mention. We support AWS/GCP KMS; HSM custody possible on Private deployments but longer lead time. For POC recommend CMK in their account (AWS KMS).
ravi (Prod): sample adapter mapping for the POC:
```yaml
adapter:
  competitor.stop_on_newline: true -> stop_sequences: ["\n"]
  competitor.stream: true -> stream: true
  competitor.max_tokens -> max_new_tokens
```
diego (Solutions): also include an A/B plan: route 10-20% of a small sandbox workload to Redwood vs CompetitorX for 24h and measure label parity and false positive rate.
maya (AE): timeline: they asked to start POC in 9 days. Is that feasible?
ravi (Prod): yes for a scoped POC (single endpoint, provided corpus, staging allowlist). We'll need POC key and network allowlist within 48h.
anya (Infra): I'll prepare Dedicated sizing options and an allowlist spreadsheet.
lee (Security): I'll upload prefilled security answers by EOD Thursday. Also flag export control and retention policy options.
ops-bot: Reminder: upload corpus and signed NDA within 72 hours to preserve POC slot.
maya (AE): action items summarized: HarborPay -> upload 40 prompts, sign NDA, provide network allowlist. Redwood -> security template (lee), token mapping + parity script (diego), infra egress and sizing (anya), adapter prototype + curl examples (ravi).
diego (Solutions): I'll deliver token mapping CSV and parity script before Friday sync.
anya (Infra): CIDRs and staging IPs shared in doc.
ravi (Prod): curl example for POC:
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/serve -H 'Authorization: Bearer $POC_KEY' -d '{"model":"redwood-lite-1","prompt":"<their prompt>","adapter":true}'
maya (AE): thanks everyone. Meeting invite for Friday 11am UTC.
